To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a residual reconstruction of video can significantly outperform block-based compressed-sensings reconstruction that ignores motion.

a) the proposed residual reconstruction for block-based compressed sensing of video is a novel, efficient, and effective reconstruction technique; b) the proposed technique is able to significantly improve the quality of compressed-sensing reconstructions of video; and c) the proposed technique achieves this quality improvement by incorporating motion estimation and compensation into the reconstruction process, and by iteratively reconstructing the frames and motion fields.

a residual reconstruction for video is superior to a block-based compressed-sensings reconstruction for still images and that a residual reconstruction that iteratively alternates between reconstruction of frames and their corresponding motion field is superior to a residual reconstruction that does so non-iteratively.
